title: Major Bones of the Human Body
description: The major bones of the human skeleton, from skull to feet, with their common names and locations.
subject: medicine-health

cards.definition: Thigh bone, running from the hip to the knee. The longest and strongest bone in the human body.
Stirrup-shaped bone of the middle ear that passes sound vibrations to the inner ear. The smallest bone in the body.
Kneecap. A bone embedded in the tendon of the quadriceps that protects the front of the knee joint.
The part of the skull that encloses and protects the brain.
Lower jawbone. It holds the lower teeth and hinges with the skull to allow chewing and speaking.
Upper jawbone. It holds the upper teeth and forms part of the hard palate.
U-shaped bone in the neck that supports the tongue. It does not form a joint with any other bone.
Collarbone. A long, S-shaped bone that connects the sternum to the scapula.
Shoulder blade. A flat, triangular bone on the upper back that connects the humerus to the clavicle.
Breastbone. A flat bone in the center of the chest that most ribs attach to through cartilage.
Twelve pairs of curved bones that form the rib cage and protect the heart and lungs.
The stacked bones of the spinal column, which support the body and protect the spinal cord.
Upper arm bone, running from the shoulder to the elbow.
Forearm bone on the thumb side.
Forearm bone on the pinky side. Its upper end forms the point of the elbow.
The eight small bones of the wrist.
The five bones of the palm, connecting the wrist to the fingers.
The bones of the fingers and toes. Each hand and each foot has 14.
Bowl-shaped ring formed by the two hip bones, sacrum, and coccyx. It supports the spine and protects pelvic organs.
Triangular bone at the base of the spine, formed from five fused vertebrae.
Tailbone. A small bone at the very bottom of the spine made of fused vertebrae.
Shinbone. The larger, weight-bearing bone of the lower leg.
The thin bone that runs alongside the tibia on the outer side of the lower leg.
The seven bones of the ankle and back of the foot, including the talus and the calcaneus (heel bone).
The five long bones of the foot between the ankle and the toes.
